Subject: Stakeholder intros & procurement path — next steps

Hi Natalie / Tom —

Thanks again for the chat today. Quick recap from our side and a set of targeted asks so we can scope a pilot and accelerate procurement: 

Summary (30 min discovery)
- Primary use case: realtime fraud scoring enrichment for checkout flows (4500 TPS expected at peak).
- Must run in us-west region; data residency stays in our cloud.
- Key decision criteria: latency at p50/p95, predictable unit cost, SOC2-compliant audit trail, and key management integration.

Asks / next steps
1) Stakeholder map: can you share a simple org chart or list of decision owners (economic buyer, engineering lead, security owner, procurement/contracting) and the preferred contact for each?
2) Procurement path: what procurement/PO process, standard contract terms, and procurement timeline should we expect? Any procurement questionnaire our legal team needs to fill out?
3) Security/legal contacts: please introduce the person who will own the security questionnaire or vendor risk review (or confirm we should reach out to procurement first).
4) Technical follow-up: would your engineering lead be available for a 30-min demo of prefix caching, batching controls, and KV lifetime? We think a short demo will answer most perf/ops questions.

For planning, we typically prepare a mutual action plan once owners are defined. If helpful I can draft an initial MAP with milestone dates (pilot sign-off, data/infra prep, go-live).

I've attached a short checklist we use for procurement (skeleton outline) — it highlights the common redlines (data retention, indemnity, export controls).

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: +1 415-555-0142 | dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_procurement_checklist_v1.pdf
